reading: A small cross-shaped exemplar on the background is erased. At each single marker cell inside the large rectangles, the exemplar's surrounding cells are stamped and its arm colour is extended as full lines (in the arm directions only) across the rectangle containing the marker; the marker cell keeps its colour.
verb: stamp exemplar and extend its arms

slots.exemplar: the small multi-coloured cross lying on the outer background (removed in output)
slots.anchors: isolated marker cells inside the rectangles
slots.lines: arm colour of the exemplar, drawn through the marker in the directions the exemplar has arms (vertical and/or horizontal), stopping at the rectangle's edges
slots.stamp: the exemplar's non-arm neighbourhood (e.g. diagonal/ring cells) copied around each marker

why: every marker gets the same exemplar pattern; lines span exactly the rectangle containing the marker; exemplar position becomes background

reading: N is the number of 8 cells in the top row. Every column whose colour in the coloured row occurs exactly N times in that row gets a bar of that colour, N cells tall, directly above the 5 separator line.

slots.N: count of 8 cells in the top row
slots.selected columns: positions in the multi-coloured row whose colour occurs exactly N times in that row
slots.bar: that column's colour, rows immediately above the separator, height N

why: bar heights all equal N; only colours with frequency N in the colour row get bars

reading: The single shape (h x w box) is arranged four times in 90-degree rotations around an empty central h x h square, giving a (2w+h) square output: original on the left, horizontal mirror on the right, transposed copy on top, its vertical flip on the bottom.

slots.unit: the input shape cropped to its box
slots.layout: left = shape, right = shape flipped left-right, top = shape transposed, bottom = transpose flipped up-down; centred on each side

why: the output has 4-fold rotational arrangement of the cropped shape with an empty centre

reading: Two full horizontal and two full vertical 8 lines cut the grid into 3x3 panels. The corner panels stay empty; top-centre is filled 2, middle-left 4, centre 6, middle-right 3, bottom-centre 1.

slots.panels: the 3x3 cells cut by the 8 separator lines
slots.colour: fixed by panel position: top-middle 2, middle-left 4, centre 6, middle-right 3, bottom-middle 1, corners 0

why: every non-corner panel is filled entirely with its position's colour

reading: The 3x3 input holds one colour in one of a few fixed shapes; the output is a single cell whose colour names the shape (2x2 block plus opposite corner -> 3, plus sign -> 6, X -> 2, the other diagonal-ish pattern 440/404/040 -> 1), regardless of the input colour.

slots.shape: the fg cell pattern of the 3x3 input, colour ignored
slots.label: lookup learned from training: {011/011/100: 3, 050/555/050: 6, 808/080/808: 2, 440/404/040: 1}

why: same fg pattern always gives same output colour

reading: Above a full 5 separator row is a multi-coloured block; the most frequent colour of that block is written into the centre cell of the bottom row.

slots.colour: most frequent colour in the panel above the separator

why: exactly one cell changes, at bottom centre, to the top panel's majority colour

reading: The 3x3 input is scaled into a 3x3 arrangement of blocks; a block holds a copy of the input wherever the input cell has the input's most frequent colour, else it is empty.
why: every output block is the input or empty; copies sit exactly at the cells of the most common input colour

reading: An empty grid is filled with a square spiral of colour 3 starting at the top-left, running clockwise inward with a one-cell gap between successive turns.

slots.path: clockwise inward spiral from (0,0) along the border, each turn leaving a 1-cell gap from the previous ring

why: output is the canonical spiral for the grid size; input is all background

reading: Each row with a coloured cell at both ends is filled: the left colour extends right and the right colour extends left until they meet, and the single middle cell becomes 5.
verb: extend ends to meet at middle

slots.source: the pair of end cells on a row
slots.fill: left half in left colour, right half in right colour

why: each line covers exactly half the row; the centre cell is 5

reading: A two-colour shape lies on one side of a full separator line of 1. A mirror copy of it, with its original colours, appears on the other side reflected across the line, while the original shape has its two colours swapped.
verb: reflect across separator and swap colours

slots.axis: the full separator line of colour 1
slots.reflection: the shape mirrored across the separator, original colours
slots.original: stays in place with its two colours exchanged (a<->b)

why: reflected copy is the exact mirror image; the original's colour swap is the 2-colour exchange of that shape
